note: Route-graph ratchet baseline (no-new-rot ratchet). Each entry is the CURRENT reachable-first-party-module-count ceiling for a LOCKED FIXED_ROUTES route (the primary dev-perf 'first-party graph pressure' metric from scripts/route-graph.mjs). The gate fails when a tracked route's count grows BEYOND its ceiling and when the committed baseline raises any ceiling vs the base branch WITHOUT a matching absorb record. Counts are captured WITH the companion extension repos cloned pinned (exactly as CI does via clone-extensions) so they reproduce in CI. Regenerate with `node scripts/audit/route-graph-ratchet.mjs --write-baseline` after cloning the extensions — a ceiling should only ever be LOWERED as barrel imports are narrowed, and is never raised SILENTLY. A sanctioned raise must be ANNOTATED: a sibling `absorbs` record `route -> { from, to, reason, pr }` whose from/to exactly match the raise vs the base branch (from = the base ceiling, to = the new committed ceiling, reason = why the growth is accepted, pr = the PR carrying the absorbed change). The gate validates records strictly (malformed/stale/orphan records fail closed; a carried-forward record may not be deleted while its raised ceiling is kept) and prints a LOUD NOTICE line for every absorbed raise. The tracked route set is route-graph.mjs FIXED_ROUTES; change it there, then regenerate.

/api/a2a.reason: cinatra#3033 (PR 3110), the forward merge of origin/main into this branch at becc5974da2ef44e95a9f6e24a3184138f172ae3, so `from` is main's OWN committed ceiling there and the whole raise is this branch's. MEASURED, NOT COMPUTED, with the companion extension fleet cloned PINNED exactly as CI clones it (116/116, missingCount 0 on every route) and FOUR trees analysed in ONE environment by the same scripts/route-graph.mjs. (1) origin/main alone at becc5974da2ef44e95a9f6e24a3184138f172ae3 lands EXACTLY on its four committed ceilings: /api/mcp 1768, /chat 1870, /api/a2a 1776, /api/llm-bridge 1786. (2) The merged tree measures /api/mcp 1795, /chat 1897, /api/a2a 1803, /api/llm-bridge 1813 — 27 more on each. (3) The merged tree with ONLY the generated renderer map (src/lib/generated/artifact-renderers.ts) returned to main's copy measures 3 more on each, isolating 24 of the 27 to the four blog packs' display leaves this slice exists to register: nine entries (blog-idea detail and preview, blog-image detail, preview and list row, blog-post detail and preview, LinkedIn detail and preview) and the extension modules each one reaches. (4) The merged tree minus ALL of this branch's leaves — that map plus src/lib/artifacts/artifact-creation.ts, src/lib/blog-image-materializer.ts, packages/agents/src/execution.ts and packages/agents/src/agentic-run-panel.tsx returned to main's copies, so the three new first-party modules those files import become unreachable — lands EXACTLY on main's four ceilings again, which closes the arithmetic: 24 display leaves, 2 for src/lib/artifacts/artifact-object-envelope.ts and src/lib/artifacts/featured-image-fields.ts, and 1 for packages/agents/src/run-failure-floor.ts. Nothing of main's is folded into this raise. /sign-in measures 163 on every tree, far under its 223 ceiling, so its ceiling and its carried-forward cinatra#2988 record stay exactly as main committed them, neither raised nor ratcheted down by this merge. Narrowing was attempted first and is unavailable: scripts/route-graph.mjs counts a dynamic import() specifier as the same first-party graph pressure as a static one, so the generated map's guarded lazy imports are already the narrowest form the metric admits, and each of the three host modules is imported for a function its importer calls at runtime, so none can become a type-only edge the analyzer erases. The PR 3302 records main committed for these four routes are RETIRED BY THIS RAISE, the one lifecycle the gate allows for an annotation whose ceiling moves.
